title: Certification harness for upgrade gates and LTS channel assurance
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: build a reusable certification harness that gates upgrades (hosted, dedicated, private) against a compact but high-value battery of checks: functional smoke runs, perf/regression statistical tests, KV cache correctness probes, and golden-prompt quality checks tied to LTS channel guarantees. This ticket codifies the end-to-end pipeline that runs pre-deploy and on canary ramps, produces a human-readable certification report, and emits machine signals that the rollout orchestrator can consume (pass/fail + confidence).

Why this is different: existing smoke and compatibility prober work validates surface compatibility; this harness explicitly ties quality/regression thresholds to release channels (stable, lts, canary) and provides deterministic acceptance criteria that combine multiple noisy signals into a single certification artifact. The harness must be lightweight (<= 10m runtime for quick preflight), configurable per-release, and auditable in Confluence and the release ticket.

Acceptance criteria:
- Small, curated test corpus ("golden prompts v2") exercised against a candidate runtime + model variant with deterministic seeding and KV-warmup flows.
- Perf regression gate: rolling statistical test comparing baseline (last LTS) to candidate with configurable alpha and minimum sample sizes. Failure modes map to remediation steps.
- KV cache correctness probe: replay of representative request prefixes to verify cache hits/evictions and deterministic output equivalence for cached prefixes.
- Canary compatibility contract checks: SDK matrix (py/ts) + protocol/response-shape validation for structured output and function-calling.
- Output: single certification JSON (and human-readable HTML) that lists checks, pass/fail, measured deltas, and links to related telemetry dashboards and PRs.
- Automation: runs as part of the pre-deploy job and can be invoked ad-hoc by SRE/PD engineers.

Notes on scope and constraints: The harness must not replace full eval suites—this is a preflight gate to catch regressions that would otherwise cause high-impact rollbacks. It should be extensible so additional probes (e.g., long-context KV stress) can be added later without changing the certification schema.
test_plan: Assemble golden prompt corpus v2 (80 prompts) with labels: safety, correctness, format, latency-sensitive
Baseline collection: run against last LTS image (runtime-1.18) to produce baseline metrics and artifacts
Candidate run: execute harness on candidate runtime image + target model variants (fp32/4bit/quantized) with 3 repeat seeds
Compute statistical regression tests for latency (p50/p95/p99) and token-accuracy on golden prompts
KV cache probe: scripted prefix replay, verify cache hit ratios and identical outputs for cached prefixes
SDK compatibility: run small matrix of py package versions (0.9.x, 1.0.x) and ts SDKs to validate request/response contract
Produce certification artifact (certification.json + certification.html) and upload to release Confluence page
runbook: If perf gate fails with p99 regression > configured threshold: mark certification 'fail', capture profiler traces, raise regression issue under release-validation backlog
If functional golden-prompt accuracy drops > 2%: fail and assign to model-onboarding + runtime teams for triage
If KV cache probe fails (mismatched outputs): block rollout to Dedicated/Private until KV determinism fixes are merged
On intermittent failures: re-run harness up to 3 times; if flakey, escalate to SRE with telemetry payload and sample traces
